GlobalVariables.StudyDescription: This file contains the metadata, events, and data for REDCap project "Access to medical oxygen scorecard (ATMOS)".

redcap:Surveys.title: Access to medical oxygen scorecard (ATMOS)
redcap:Surveys.instructions:
This scorecard supports governments in monitoring and reporting progress on the World Health Organization resolution 76.3, Increasing access to medical oxygen. It has been developed and adapted from a tool created by the Lancet Global Health Commission on medical oxygen security.

The revised ATMO₂S scorecard includes performance indicators aligned with all components of the WHO oxygen resolution.

For additional technical guidance on oxygen systems, please refer to the WHO Access to Oxygen Initiative webpage: https://www.who.int/initiatives/oxygen-access-scale-up

The survey is divided into four sections:

    1. Oxygen architecture
    2. Oxygen availability
    3. Oxygen affordability
    4. Oxygen adoption

At the end of the survey, you will receive a score representing the sum of your responses to all self-assessment questions. You will also have the option to save your responses for your records.

Question.redcap:FormattedTranslatedText:
Item

"We have systems in place to ensure appropriate use of oxygen among those who need it."

Details

Systems refer to guidelines that guide clinical care, and accountability mechanisms that ensure quality of care (including safe use of medical oxygen). Appropriate use of medical oxygen refers to both the safe delivery of medical oxygen to the patient, and the diagnosis and monitoring of patients using pulse oximetry. Where possible, the score should be data driven. Without data, evidence of systems should be used and discussed qualitatively.

Potential sources of evidence:

  • National clinical guidelines for medical oxygen use (adapted to different cadres and health system levels).

  • Standard operating procedures for use and maintenance of medical equipment and other devices.

  • Facility audits for oxygen production and distribution equipment; up-to-date inventory of functional equipment.

  • Patient surveys.

  • Adverse event data for patients (e.g. neonatal retinopathy).

  • Adverse event data for systems or equipment.

3 = A pandemic preparedness plan exists, and medical oxygen is adequately considered across multiple scenarios.

2 = Some coordination mechanisms in place, but their ability to impact oxygen access is limited (e.g. lack reach, partially active, lack leadership).
3 = Several currently active mechanisms exist to support coordination, with a person(s)/agency responsible for national oxygen coordination.
1 = Health infrastructure policy does not exist, or if it does, it makes no allowance for medical oxygen or other medical gas systems.

3 = Systems are in place to track and report medical oxygen production, distribution and need, and that supply has met need over the prior calendar year.

3 = Medical oxygen is included in plans and guidelines for various different scenarios that would require surge capacity, and supply has met need over the prior calendar year.
1 = Quantification of medical oxygen need is not conducted.

2 = Regulatory instruments and standards for medical oxygen, respiratory care medical devices and associated equipment exist, but they are insufficient or lack oversight.
